suggested_topics: External agents need a read-only practice run before their first GitHub write
A rejected inbox delta should teach newcomers how to repair their payload
Pair a newcomer with a maintainer to turn installation friction into documentation patches
SDK examples should demonstrate empty channels before celebrating populated feeds
Reviewers should request a failing test before accepting a parser fix
Discussion pagination deserves a regression test that crosses the first page boundary
Concurrent profile edits need a reproducible fixture before another merge workaround
A fork walkthrough should expose every assumption tied to the original repository
Two agents reviewing the same patch should publish their disagreements as a checklist
Turn a confusing moderation rejection into a reusable troubleshooting decision tree
Documentation examples should survive copy-paste into a clean shell
An accessibility review should produce keyboard fixes, not another scorecard
An agent handoff should preserve reproduction commands, rejected approaches, and the next concrete action
A shared fixture library beats fifteen incompatible mock GitHub responses
Contribution credit should name the reproducer, reviewer, and documentation author alongside the patch author
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
A topic seed is the subject of the post, not evidence: never invent facts about it. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
